name: Web Data Collection
title: Web Data Collection
answer: Web data collection is the practice of gathering information from public websites and web services for use as alternative data. It covers prices, product listings, job postings, reviews, app rankings, shipping notices, and other signals that are not available in standard market or economic datasets. The output is usually a structured time series or panel that can be joined to company, sector, or geographic identifiers. It sits in alternative data because it offers a real time or high frequency view that traditional sources may lag.

sections.body: Web data collection is the practice of gathering information from public websites and web services for use as alternative data. It covers prices, product listings, job postings, reviews, app rankings, shipping notices, and other signals that are not available in standard market or economic datasets. The output is usually a structured time series or panel that can be joined to company, sector, or geographic identifiers. It sits in alternative data because it offers a real time or high frequency view that traditional sources may lag.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a stack of crawlers, headless browsers, and scheduled jobs that fetch pages or call APIs. Proxies, rotating IP addresses, and rate limiting help manage load and reduce blocking. Storage and processing often sit in cloud object stores and databases, with queues for retries and monitoring for failures. Some teams use open source frameworks and commercial scraping services, while others build custom pipelines.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A typical pipeline starts with target selection and a crawl plan, then fetches pages, parses the relevant fields, and normalizes values into a common schema. Deduplication and entity resolution link records to the right company, product, or location. Quality checks compare samples against source pages, track coverage over time, and flag gaps or sudden changes. The result is a documented dataset with timestamps and source URLs for each observation.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk around web data collection turn on terms of service, robots.txt, copyright, database rights, and personal data rules such as GDPR and CCPA. Provenance matters because a dataset is only as defensible as its audit trail, which records what was collected, when, from where, and under what basis. The site tracks 148 active AI lawsuits and 219 compliance and regulation pages, a sign that legal questions around data sourcing remain active. Teams often separate public, nonpersonal data from any personal data and apply retention limits and access controls. Contracts with data vendors commonly spell out permitted use, resale, and indemnity, though this page does not give legal advice.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward more API first access, licensed feeds, and partnerships that reduce reliance on raw scraping. Browser automation and anti bot measures will keep evolving, so collection teams invest in resilience and legal review. Demand is growing for provenance metadata, consent records, and reproducible pipelines that can be audited. Some collection may shift to synthetic or aggregated sources where direct web data is too costly or too risky to obtain.
